title: LSASS memory accessed with full-access masks by PowerShell.exe on scranton and wsmprovhost.exe on nashua
summary: On 2020-05-02 at 03:05:16, PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton.dmevals.local opened lsass.exe (PID 736) with GrantedAccess 0x1FFFFF (PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) and 0x1f3fff, with a CallTrace ending in an UNKNOWN module (UNKNOWN(000001996D28200D)) rather than a signed system DLL — the classic signature of an in-memory LSASS dump. The same access mask 0x1f3fff against lsass.exe was used by wsmprovhost.exe (WinRM remote PowerShell) on nashua.dmevals.local at 03:09:29. This occurred in the middle of a post-exploitation PowerShell toolkit run by user pbeesly on scranton (Invoke-Discovery, Invoke-Persistence, Get-PrivateKeys, Invoke-ScreenCapture, Get-Keystrokes, Invoke-Exfil loaded from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\psversion.ps1). The Windows security log independently records pbeesly's powershell.exe accessing \Device\HarddiskVolume2\Windows\System32\lsass.exe at 03:05:16. The 0x1000 accesses by svchost.exe and the 0x1fffff accesses by wininit.exe/csrss.exe at 03:19:09 are normal system behaviour (boot-time), but the PowerShell/wsmprovhost accesses with read-memory masks are not.

title: No SAM/SECURITY hive dumping observed
summary: No evidence of SAM/SECURITY registry hive dumping was found. Searches for reg save / esentutl / vssadmin command lines, SAM/SECURITY file writes, and 4663 access to SAM objects returned no hits. The only SAM-related object types seen (SAM_DOMAIN, SAM_SERVER, SAM_ALIAS) appeared in the general 4663/4656/4670 object-type stack but no 4663 event with a SAM ObjectName was retrieved, and the three file-create events matching *SAM*/*SECURITY*/*SYSTEM* were benign Prefetch files (SECURITYHEALTHSYSTRAY.EXE-41AD6DE1.pf etc.) created by svchost.exe. The credential theft on these hosts was via LSASS memory, not offline hive extraction.

title: Azure Network Watcher agent runs netsh trace capture on scranton (benign)
summary: On scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-01T23:19:17-04:00, netsh.exe was launched with 'trace start capture=yes traceFile=...etl'. The parent process is the Microsoft Azure NetworkWatcherAgent (NetworkWatcherAgent.exe), and the surrounding process chain is the Azure Guest Agent lifecycle (WaAppAgent.exe logman stop/create/start of GAEvents/RTEvents, GuestAgent enable.cmd, NetworkWatcherAgent Install/Start). This is the platform's built-in network monitoring agent, not an adversary packet sniffer.

title: No packet-sniffing tooling observed on any Windows host
summary: Across windows.sysmon process-creation (event.code:1) and windows.security 4688, no execution of windump, tcpdump, wireshark, dumpcap, pktmon, rawcap, NetworkMiner or Npcap was found (queries returned 0 hits). No pcap/Npcap driver image-load (event.code:6) was observed either. The only capture-related binary is the legitimate Azure NetworkWatcherAgent/netsh pair. No PowerShell script block (4104) referenced sniffing, capture, pcap, promiscuous or netsh. There is no host-based evidence of network sniffing.

title: Zeek 'weird' records are sensor-side capture artifacts, not a sniffer on the wire
summary: The 12 zeek weird records on observers simplerockbuild.simplerock.lan and bobs.bigwheel.local are ip_hdr_len_zero, truncated_IP and unknown_dce_rpc_auth_type events, plus two SSL::Invalid_Server_Cert notices. These are normal Zeek parsing anomalies (malformed/truncated packets and self-signed certs), not indicators of a promiscuous-mode sniffer. The zeek window (2020-04-30) does not overlap the Windows host activity (2020-05-02), so it cannot be correlated to the credential-theft campaign.

title: Concurrent malicious activity is credential theft/lateral movement, not sniffing
summary: While no sniffing occurred, the same window shows a real intrusion: user pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local ran PsExec64.exe with a plaintext password ('-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by') to launch C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on \\NASHUA (PSEXESVC service installed repeatedly), and sdelete64.exe was used to wipe files including C:\programdata\victim\???cod.3aka3.scr. The python.exe payload on nashua.dmevals.local made repeated outbound connections to 192.168.0.4:8443. This is credential access/lateral movement (not T1040) and is reported here only as context; it does not constitute network sniffing.

title: PowerShell screen-capture function (Invoke-ScreenCapture) run by pbeesly on scranton
summary: On 2020-05-02 at 03:05:53 UTC on scranton.dmevals.local, user pbeesly (S-1-5-21-1830255721-3727074217-2423397540-1107) defined and then invoked a PowerShell function 'Invoke-ScreenCapture' (script block path C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\psversion.ps1). title: No brute-force authentication activity observed; credential activity is theft, not guessing
summary: Across windows.security (41002 events, 02:55-03:28Z), windows.sysmon, windows.powershell and windows.other there is no evidence of repeated failed authentication. Event 4625 (failed logon) has zero hits, and the only 4771/4776-family event is a single successful NTLM validation (4776, Status 0x0) for pbeesly on newyork.dmevals.local. The C077/C085 hits (svchost.exe, conhost.exe, netsh.exe, userinit.exe command lines containing 'net'/'user'/'runas') are ordinary Windows service and shell command lines, not scripted authentication attempts. The genuine credential-access activity on scranton.dmevals.local (pbeesly) is credential theft/export (private-key export, LSASS handle access), which is outside the T1110 brute-force family.

title: No password-guessing activity; runas/net use hits are benign system processes
summary: The C085 aggregate of processes with 'runas'/'net use' in the command line is dominated by legitimate Windows binaries (svchost.exe 100, conhost.exe 65, backgroundTaskHost.exe 18, WmiPrvSE.exe 17, RuntimeBroker.exe 13, taskhostw.exe 13). No interactive credential-guessing tooling appears. windows.security has zero 4625 failed-logon events and no 4771 Kerberos pre-auth failures; the only Kerberos error in zeek is KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED (7), which is a normal pre-auth negotiation, not a failure. No evidence of password guessing.

title: No password-cracking tooling; LSASS access is a single low-privilege handle, not hash dumping
summary: No hashcat/john/crack command lines exist (C088 zero hits) and no cracking output files (.pot/.hash) were created (C089 only shows benign .txt files such as WER temp files and Sysinternals readme.txt). The 326 lsass-targeted Sysmon event 10 accesses are overwhelmingly from svchost.exe (289) and Azure antimalware/telemetry agents (AntimalwareConfig.exe 15, WindowsAzureTelemetryService.exe 13) - normal security-product behaviour. Only 2 accesses come from powershell.exe on scranton.dmevals.local with GrantedAccess 0x1000 (PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), which is not the memory-read access used for credential dumping. Registry hive reads (C091/C092) are by lsass.exe itself, i.e. normal. No cracking evidence.

title: No password spraying; 4648 explicit-credential logons are PsExec-driven lateral movement by pbeesly
summary: The 15 event-4648 explicit-credential logons are all for the single account pbeesly, alternating between scranton.dmevals.local (SubjectUserName pbeesly, IpAddress 10.0.1.6, TargetServerName NASHUA) and nashua.dmevals.local (SubjectUserName NASHUA$, ProcessName C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe). This is one account being reused across hosts via PsExec, not many accounts tried against one host, so it does not match spraying. There are zero 4625 failures and no 4771 pre-auth failures. The pattern is consistent with lateral movement using stolen credentials rather than password spraying.

title: No credential stuffing; PowerShell credential use is hardcoded, not list-driven
summary: No process was launched with a credential-list file argument (C108: only logman.exe with a .txt, a benign logging utility). The PowerShell 4104 hits referencing Credential/ConvertTo-SecureString are hardcoded single credentials, not imported credential lists: on scranton.dmevals.local pbeesly ran Get-PrivateKeys using ConvertTo-SecureString -String "saribas" to export machine private keys, and Invoke-Exfil using a hardcoded PSCredential (cozy / MyCozyPassw0rd!) to map a WebDAV share. These are credential theft/exfiltration, not stuffing of stolen credential pairs against many accounts.
